title: NTD-identification
text: create DGP : Two genders: women men (men earning ) Two treatment cohorts: early (D=25) late (D=30) Linear earnings growth, late cohorts steeper slopes Earnings penalties childbirth key feature: taking ratios within gender, difference men women netted
code: # Parameters baseline    <- 500 ratio_bias  <- 3    # late vs early slope multiplier ratio_apos  <- 3    # men vs women slope multiplier ages        <- 20:30 d_early     <- 25 d_late      <- 30  # Counterfactual earning slopes s_f_25 <- baseline s_f_30 <- baseline * ratio_bias s_m_25 <- baseline * ratio_apos s_m_30 <- baseline * ratio_apos * ratio_bias  # Treatment effects (ATT) att_f  <- -6000 att_m  <- -2000  # Build each group make_group <- function(sex, D, slope, att_level) {   tibble(     age    = ages,     female = sex,     D      = D,     y_0    = slope * age,           # counterfactual (no treatment)     y_1    = y_0 + ifelse(age >= D, att_level, 0),     y      = y_1                     # observed   ) }  data <- bind_rows(   make_group(1, d_early, s_f_25, att_f),   make_group(1, d_late,  s_f_30, att_f),   make_group(0, d_early, s_m_25, att_m),   make_group(0, d_late,  s_m_30, att_m) )

title: NTD-identification
text: First, let’s calculate parallel trend violation levels - difference counterfactual trends early late treated within gender:  parallel trends violations levels equal across gender. Men’s violations much larger higher earnings. violates difference--differences (), assumes violation, triple differences (TD), assumes equal violations levels across genders.
code: # Calculate trend from pre-treatment (age D-1) to each subsequent age trends <- function(g, d, a) {   pre <- data |> filter(D == d, female == g, age == d-1) |> pull(y_0)   post <- data |> filter(D == d, female == g, age == a) |> pull(y_0)   post - pre }  # Difference in trends between early and late cohorts diff_trends <- function(g, a) trends(g, 25, a) - trends(g, 30, a)  expand_grid(   female = c(0, 1),   age    = ages ) |>   mutate(     diff_trend = purrr::map2_dbl(female, age, diff_trends),     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men"))   ) |>    ggplot(aes(x = age, y = diff_trend, color = gender)) +    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +    labs(     title = "Parallel Trends Violation in Levels by Gender",     x = "Age",      y = "Difference in counterfactual trends",      color = "Gender"   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

text: Now let’s normalize dividing average potential earnings (APO — average potential outcome, counterfactual earnings absent children) absence treatment:  Takeaway: normalized parallel trends violations identical men women every age. exactly NTD identification assumption requires. work? construction, late cohort slopes constant multiple early slopes (within gender), men’s slopes constant multiple women’s slopes (within cohort). constant multiples men cancel take ratios, ensuring normalized PT violations equal across gender. –
code: # Get counterfactual earnings for early cohort (APO) get_apo <- function(g, a) {   data |>     dplyr::filter(D == 25, female == g, age == a) |>     dplyr::pull(y_0) }  expand_grid(   female = c(0, 1),   age    = ages ) |>   mutate(     diff_trend = purrr::map2_dbl(female, age, diff_trends),     y_0 = purrr::map2_dbl(female, age, get_apo),     norm_diff_trend = diff_trend / y_0,     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men"))   ) |>    ggplot(aes(x = age, y = norm_diff_trend, color = gender)) +    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +    labs(     title = "Normalized Parallel Trends Violation",     x = "Age",      y = "Normalized difference in counterfactual trends",      color = "Gender"   ) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: The Setup - Counterfactuals and Observed Data
title: NTD-identification
text: Let’s start seeing observe vs. true counterfactuals:  solid blue line shows observe early cohort treatment age 25 Light blue dashed: happened without treatment (early cohort) Orange dashed: counterfactual late treatment group gap solid light blue dashed = average treatment effect (ATE) problem: don’t observe light blue line. need impute somehow.
code: plot_df <- bind_rows(   # Early cohort: observed and counterfactual   data %>%     filter(D == d_early) %>%     pivot_longer(cols = c(y_0, y), names_to = "series", values_to = "value"),   # Late cohort: counterfactual only (not yet treated at these ages for early cohort)   data %>%     filter(D == d_late) %>%     transmute(age, female, D, series = "y_0", value = y_0) ) %>%   mutate(     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men")),     cohort = factor(if_else(D == d_early, "Early (D=25)", "Late (D=30)"),                     levels = c("Early (D=25)", "Late (D=30)")),     series_label = case_when(       cohort == "Early (D=25)" & series == "y"   ~ "Early — Observed",       cohort == "Early (D=25)" & series == "y_0" ~ "Early — Counterfactual",       cohort == "Late (D=30)"  & series == "y_0" ~ "Late — Counterfactual"     ),     linetype = if_else(series_label == "Early — Observed", "solid", "dashed"),     color = case_when(       series_label == "Early — Observed"       ~ "Obs.",       series_label == "Early — Counterfactual" ~ "CF Early",       TRUE                                     ~ "CF Late"     )   )  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = age, y = value, group = series_label)) +   geom_line(aes(linetype = linetype, color = color), linewidth = 1.1) +   facet_wrap(~ gender, nrow = 1) +   scale_linetype_identity() +   scale_color_manual(     values = c("Obs." = "#1f77b4", "CF Early" = "#9ecae1", "CF Late" = "#fdae6b")   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 1: Observed vs. Counterfactual Earnings",     x = "Age", y = "Earnings", color = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: The DID Approach - Using Late Cohort as Control
title: NTD-identification
text: uses trend late cohort impute counterfactual early cohort:  green line (imputed counterfactual) doesn’t match light blue line (true counterfactual). difference bias due parallel trend violations. happens late cohort steeper slope counterfactual earnings.
code: # Calculate DID-imputed counterfactual did_cf <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 0), function(g) {   # Early cohort's pre-treatment level   early_pre <- data %>%     filter(female == g, D == d_early, age == d_early - 1) %>%     pull(y)      # Late cohort trend   late_cf <- data %>% filter(female == g, D == d_late) %>% select(age, y_0)   late_pre <- late_cf %>% filter(age == d_early - 1) %>% pull(y_0)      # DID imputation: shift late trend to match early pre-treatment level   tibble(     age    = late_cf$age,     female = g,     D      = d_early,     series = "y_cf_did",     value  = early_pre + (late_cf$y_0 - late_pre)   ) })) %>%   mutate(     gender = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men")),     cohort = factor("Early (D=25)", levels = c("Early (D=25)", "Late (D=30)")),     series_label = "Early — DID-imputed CF",     linetype = "dotdash",     color = "CF DID"   )  plot_df_plus <- bind_rows(plot_df, did_cf)  ggplot(plot_df_plus, aes(x = age, y = value, group = series_label)) +   geom_line(aes(linetype = linetype, color = color), linewidth = 1.1) +   facet_wrap(~ gender, nrow = 1) +   scale_linetype_identity() +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(       "Obs." = "#1f77b4", "CF Early" = "#9ecae1",        "CF Late" = "#fdae6b", "CF DID" = "#2ca02c"     )   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 2: DID-Imputed Counterfactual",     subtitle = "Green line = what DID thinks would have happened without treatment",     x = "Age", y = "Earnings", color = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: Decomposing DID Estimates into Truth and Bias
title: NTD-identification
text: Let’s break gives us. First, figure, : APO (green line) Truth APO (light blue line) ATE (difference observed earnings green line) Truth ATE (difference observed earnings light blue line) PT Bias (difference green light blue lines) age, can decompose: APO = True APO + PT Bias ATE = True ATE - PT Bias (ATE difference orange green lines, PT bias comes minus) , calculate APO ATE . show decomposition value, age gender, truth bias.  surprising: counterfactual trends equal, identify APO, hence doesn’t identify ATE.
code: # Calculate true APO and ATE early_true_age <- data %>%   filter(D == d_early) %>%   group_by(female, age) %>%   summarise(APO_true = y_0, APO_obs = y, .groups = "drop") |>    mutate(ATE_true = APO_obs - APO_true)  # Calculate DID APO early_did_age <- did_cf %>%   group_by(female, age) %>%   summarise(APO_did = value, .groups = "drop")  # Combine and calculate bias summary_age <- early_true_age %>%   left_join(early_did_age, by = c("female", "age")) %>%   mutate(     PT_bias = APO_did - APO_true,  # parallel trends bias     ATE_did = APO_obs - APO_did,  # DID ATE = truth - PT bias     gender  = factor(if_else(female == 1, "Women", "Men"), levels = c("Women", "Men"))   )  # Prepare stacked bar chart data apo_stack_age <- summary_age %>%   transmute(     gender, age = factor(age),     measure = factor("APO", levels = c("APO", "ATE")),     total = APO_did, comp_true = APO_true, comp_bias = PT_bias   ) %>%   pivot_longer(c(comp_true, comp_bias), names_to = "component", values_to = "value") %>%   mutate(component = if_else(component == "comp_true", "Truth", "PT bias"))  ate_stack_age <- summary_age %>%   transmute(     gender, age = factor(age),     measure = factor("ATE", levels = c("APO", "ATE")),     total = ATE_did, comp_true = ATE_true, comp_bias = -PT_bias   ) %>%   pivot_longer(c(comp_true, comp_bias), names_to = "component", values_to = "value") %>%   mutate(component = if_else(component == "comp_true", "Truth", "PT bias"))  bar_age_df <- bind_rows(apo_stack_age, ate_stack_age)  ggplot(bar_age_df, aes(x = age, y = value, fill = component)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   facet_grid(rows = vars(measure), cols = vars(gender), scales = "free_y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("Truth" = "#1f77b4", "PT bias" = "#fdae6b"),     breaks = c("Truth", "PT bias")   ) +   labs(     title = "Decomposing DID into effect and bias",     subtitle = "Top row: DID APO | Bottom row: DID ATE",     x = "Age", y = NULL, fill = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

theta_true * (PT_bias / APO_did)   )  theta_stack <- bind_rows(   theta_df %>% transmute(     gender, age, measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     component = "Truth", value = theta_true   ),   theta_df %>% transmute(     gender, age, measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     component = "Bias A", value = bias_A   ),   theta_df %>% transmute(     gender, age, measure = factor("Ratios", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios")),     component = "Bias B", value = bias_B   ) )  bar_age_three3 <- bind_rows(   apo_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("APO", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   ate_stack_age %>% mutate(measure = factor("ATE", levels = c("APO","ATE","Ratios"))),   theta_stack )  ggplot(bar_age_three3, aes(x = age, y = value, fill = component)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   facet_grid(rows = vars(measure), cols = vars(gender), scales = "free_y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c(       "Truth" = "#1f77b4", "PT bias" = "#fdae6b",       "Bias A" = "#99d8c9", "Bias B" = "#2ca25f"     ),     breaks = c("Truth", "PT bias", "Bias A", "Bias B"),     labels = c("Truth", "PT bias", "PT / DID APO", "Truth × Bias")   ) +   labs(     title = "Figure 6: The Multiplicative Bias Structure",     subtitle = "Bottom row: Blue (true θ) + Teal (drops out) + Green (multiplicative bias)",     x = "Age", y = NULL, fill = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: aggregate-estimands
text: multiple_treatment_group_analysis() estimates child-penalty effects separately treatment group dd (age first birth). groups differ baseline earnings, age composition, selection, single group’s estimate directly comparable another’s. aggregate_estimands() collapses group-specific estimates single number per event time, answering question: average effect across distribution first-birth ages? Three aggregate estimands available: avg_of_ratios (θAgg,1\theta_{\text{Agg},1}): weighted average group’s normalized effect θ(g,d,d+e)\theta(g,d,d+e). Formally, θAgg,1(g,e)=∑dwd⋅θ(g,d,d+e)\theta_{\text{Agg},1}(g,e) = \sum_d w_d \cdot \theta(g,d,d+e), wdw_d population weights normalised sum one. Preferred normalization happens within group aggregation, baseline differences inflate average. ratio_of_avgs (θAgg,2\theta_{\text{Agg},2}): ratio weighted-average ATE weighted-average APO. Formally, θAgg,2(g,e)=∑dwd⋅ATE(g,d,d+e)/∑dwd⋅APO(g,d,d+e)\theta_{\text{Agg},2}(g,e) = \sum_d w_d \cdot \text{ATE}(g,d,d+e) \;/\; \sum_d w_d \cdot \text{APO}(g,d,d+e). implicitly -weights high-earning groups (larger APO contributes proportionally pooled denominator), differs θAgg,1\theta_{\text{Agg},1} earnings vary across groups. gender_ineq (ΔρAgg\Delta\rho_{\text{Agg}}): weighted average NTD_New Δρ\Delta\rho estimates — aggregate gender-inequality penalty. Formally, ΔρAgg(e)=∑dwd⋅Δρ(d,d+e)\Delta\rho_{\text{Agg}}(e) = \sum_d w_d \cdot \Delta\rho(d,d+e).

title: aggregate-estimands
text: default treatment groups receive equal weight. Researchers often want weight groups empirical share target population. contrast two stylized distributions: Right-skewed (mimicking US): first births concentrate younger ages. Left-skewed (mimicking Southern Europe): first births concentrate older ages.  younger groups bear larger penalties older groups (vice versa), choice weight vector shifts aggregate estimate. Reporting provides sensitivity check much aggregate depends first-birth distribution.

title: Estimation
text: childpen provides five estimators child penalty earnings: DID_Female, DID_Male, TD, NTD_Conv, NTD_New. five computed jointly single call multiple_treatment_group_analysis(), returns one row per treatment group ×\times event time ×\times estimand ×\times method combination. estimators differ target: DID_Female / DID_Male — gender-specific average treatment effects, using closest -yet-treated group control. TD — gender gap treatment effects (levels), .e. ATE(female) − ATE(male). NTD_Conv — conventional child penalty: gender gap normalised effects, θf−θm\theta_f - \theta_m. NTD_New — effect parenthood gender earnings ratio ρ\rho, denoted Δρ\Delta\rho.

title: Estimation
text: NTD produces two estimands measure gender gap normalised terms. NTD_Conv gap normalised effects — conventional child penalty: NTD_Conv(d,d′,)=δθ(f,d,d′,)−δθ(m,d,d′,).\mathrm{NTD\_Conv}(d, d^\prime, ) = \delta_{\theta}(f, d, d^\prime, ) - \delta_{\theta}(m, d, d^\prime, ). NTD_New measures effect parenthood gender earnings ratio ρ\rho: NTD_New(d,d′,)=𝔼[Ya∣f,D=d]𝔼[Ya∣m,D=d]−δAPO(f,d,d′,)δAPO(m,d,d′,)=Δρ.\mathrm{NTD\_New}(d, d^\prime, ) = \frac{\mathbb{E}[Y_a \mid f, D=d]}{\mathbb{E}[Y_a \mid m, D=d]} - \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(f, d, d^\prime, )}{\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(m, d, d^\prime, )} = \Delta\rho. use NTD_Conv vs NTD_New: NTD_Conv normalises gender’s ATE pre-birth earnings level, comparable across groups different baseline earnings. NTD_New instead asks much ratio female--male earnings changes parenthood, making directly interpretable change gender earnings ratio.

title: Aggregate estimands across treatment groups — aggregate_estimands
text: avg_of_ratios (\(\theta_{\text{Agg},1}\)) Weighted average group-specific normalised effects \(\theta(g, d, d+e)\) across treatment groups \(d\).  preferred estimand averages effects already scaled group's baseline. ratio_of_avgs (\(\theta_{\text{Agg},2}\)) Ratio weighted-average ATE weighted-average APO.  implicit weight group \(p_d \cdot \text{APO}_d\), giving higher-earning groups influence. gender_ineq (\(\Delta\rho_{\text{Agg}}\)) Weighted average NTD_New (estimand == "Delta_rho") across treatment groups – aggregate gender-inequality estimand. Standard errors.  raw influence functions stored results object, SEs computed treating group-specific estimates mutually independent. avg_of_ratios: $$\mathrm{SE}(\hat\theta_{\text{Agg},1}) = \sqrt{\sum_d w_d^2 \, \hat\sigma_d^2}$$ ratio_of_avgs, delta method applied ratio \(\bar\mu_{\text{ATE}} / \bar\mu_{\text{APO}}\): $$\mathrm{SE} \approx \frac{1}{\bar\mu_{\text{APO}}}   \sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(\bar\mu_{\text{ATE}}) +         \hat\theta_{\text{Agg},2}^2 \, \mathrm{Var}(\bar\mu_{\text{APO}})}$$ variances computed via independent-groups formula. Handling missing cells.  every treatment group produces estimate every event time (due max_age / min_age bounds).  function operates whichever groups present cell reports many via n_groups.  weights supplied, entries whose names appear observed treatment groups used; remaining weights dropped retained weights renormalised.

title: Unconditional estimands for a single treatment group — single_treatment_group_analysis
text: Let \(Y(, g, d^\star)\) denote mean outcome age \(\) gender \(g \\{0,1\}\) (1 = female) assigned group \(d^\star\). core components : APO(g; d, d', ) \(= Y(d-\mathrm{pre}, g, d) + Y(, g, d') - Y(d-\mathrm{pre}, g, d')\) ATE(g; d, d', ) \(= Y(, g, d) - \mathrm{APO}(g; d, d', )\) \(\theta\)(g) \(= \mathrm{ATE}(g) / \mathrm{APO}(g)\) , cross-gender contrasts formed: TD \(= \mathrm{ATE}(F) - \mathrm{ATE}(M)\) NTD_Conv \(= \theta(F) - \theta(M)\) NTD_New \(= \frac{Y(,F,d)}{Y(,M,d)} - \frac{\mathrm{APO}(F)}{\mathrm{APO}(M)}\) TD Null NTD_Conv_Null variants defined analogously null-effect--fathers bias-correction. Internally, influence functions pieces written temporary columns data.table via compute_mean_if(), cluster-robust standard errors computed summing IFs id level via se_cluster().
